approvals.approval: Place of Entertainment, Limited Live Performance or Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit

basis.text: A live performance, a DJ or karaoke needs a Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (one performer without amplification who ends by 10 p.m. needs none). Regular amplified sound outdoors needs a Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit. The Entertainment Commission holds a public hearing on each application. Recorded music indoors with no performer needs no entertainment permit, and dancing by patrons needs no permit of its own. Where a permit is needed: further review.
basis.code_section: San Francisco Police Code § 1060 et seq. (Place of Entertainment; Limited Live Performance; Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound)

expected_conditions.condition: Operating hours shall not extend beyond 1 a.m. Sunday through Saturday.
expected_conditions.basis: The CUA application describes a 1 a.m. closing time, which falls within principally permitted hours. Planning routinely conditions CUAs to match the applicant's proposed hours and caps them to prevent later expansion without amendment. Comparable CUAs in NCT-VALENCIA and NCT-MISSION cap hours to match the application.

expected_conditions.condition: The Place of Entertainment permit shall limit live entertainment to the performance area shown on the approved floor plan, and sound levels at the property line shall not exceed 55 dBA between 10 p.m. and 7 a.m.
expected_conditions.basis: Entertainment Commission conditions routinely cap sound levels at the property line to protect neighboring residences. The 55 dBA nighttime limit is a common threshold in POE permits for venues in mixed-use districts; the 2026-006164PRL record notes Good Neighbor Policy enforcement for nightlife at 2500 Mission.

expected_conditions.condition: A security plan shall be submitted to the Entertainment Commission and the Police Department, detailing staffing, ID checks, crowd control and incident reporting, and the plan shall be updated annually.
expected_conditions.basis: POE permits in the Mission and Valencia corridors typically require a security plan reviewed by SFPD. The Entertainment Commission imposes this condition to address late-night safety and neighbor concerns; the catalog entry for the POE permit notes Police referral and review.

comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning distinguished continuation of a restaurant Type 41 from establishment of a bar use. The 2008 approval was an agency referral (not a full CUA), underscoring that a change of use from restaurant to bar triggers conditional-use review even when the existing license remains.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm with SF Planning's Conditional Use coordinator whether a Type 42 license from a bar inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD is available for transfer to 995 Valencia St and obtain a written statement that the transfer meets § 249.60(b)(2)(C).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Contact Planning by email or phone and explain that you are preparing a CUA application for a beer-and-wine bar at 995 Valencia and need to confirm which Type 42 or Type 48 licenses inside the Mission SUD are available for transfer. Ask whether Planning has a list of licenses that satisfy the in-district transfer requirement, and request written confirmation that a specific license (once identified) meets the Code. Without this confirmation, the CUA cannot proceed.

filing_playbook.action: Retain an architect to prepare a code analysis and measured floor plan showing the bar layout, the limited kitchen, the performance area, and the occupant load, and submit the analysis with the CUA application to confirm that no Building Code change of occupancy is triggered if the occupant load is…
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The architect should calculate the occupant load per California Building Code 2025 § 1004, classify the proposed use (Assembly A-2 if occupant load ≥ 50, Business B if < 50), and state whether the existing occupancy group (if known) matches the proposed group. If the load is under 50 and the space is already Group B or A-2, no change of occupancy is required and the building permit is simpler. Include the floor plan and code memo in the CUA application so Planning can see that the 40-seat count does not misrepresent the actual load.

timeline_cost.notes: The day and cost ranges cover the Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days, $3,100–$15,000 per catalog:sf.conditional_use_authorization), the Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days, $2,708–$3,800 per catalog:sf.place_of_entertainment_permit), the ABC Type 42 license transfer (60–150 days, $1,000–$1,600 per catalog:ca.abc_type_42), the Health Permit to Operate (14–45 days, $470–$1,000 per catalog:sf.health_permit plus $828–$2,500 for plan check per catalog:sf.health_plan_check), and the building permit (14–120 days, $800–$15,000 per catalog:sf.building_permit, filed in parallel with health plan check). These are times to approval for cases that are approved; they do not include denials, withdrawals or purchase of the Type 42 license itself. The CUA is the critical path: 120–300 days includes pre-application community meeting, environmental review, hearing scheduling, the hearing, and the 30-day appeal period. The ABC transfer timeline assumes no Public Convenience or Necessity hearing; if census tract 208.01's over-quota status triggers a PCN referral to the Board of Supervisors, add 60–90 days. The POE permit (45–120 days) begins after the CUA is final and includes the Entertainment Commission's referral to Police, Planning, Public Health and Fire, the 30-day posted notice, and the hearing. The building permit and health permit can proceed in parallel once the CUA is approved, but DBI will not issue the building permit, and DPH will not issue the health permit, until Planning confirms that construction and operations conform to the CUA conditions. The cost range does not include the purchase price of the Type 42 license (typically $15,000–$75,000 in San Francisco, depending on availability and seller), the architect's fees for plans and code analysis, the acoustic consultant's soundproofing plan, the ABC broker's commission, or construction costs. The timeline also excludes the time to identify and escrow a Type 42 license from a bar inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD, which can take 30–90 days depending on market availability.

records_summary: 995 Valencia St is zoned NCT-VALENCIA and sits inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District, which requires that any new bar use transfer a liquor license from another bar already inside the district. The pathway shows this concept is a change of use from Restaurant (currently operating as Sarita's Grill & Beer with an active Type 41 license) to Bar, requiring a Conditional Use Authorization. The 1 a.m. closing falls within principally permitted hours. Within 500 ft there are 9 active on-sale ABC licenses and 24 registered food/drink businesses, flagging potential undue-concentration concerns. Only 3 dated use decisions in the last 10 years within 1,000 ft—too few for a meaningful approval rate—but the site history shows continuous restaurant approvals here since 1999, and nearby CUAs for restaurants with alcohol have been approved.
